Don’t push through shoulder pain when pressing. Stop that movement for now and avoid any exercise that causes sharp, worsening, or persistent pain. You can try gentle, pain-free range-of-motion and consider getting assessed by a qualified clinician or physiotherapist—especially if it keeps returning.

Seek urgent care if the pain followed a major injury, or you have sudden weakness, inability to lift your arm, visible deformity, marked swelling, numbness/tingling, chest pain, or shortness of breath. If you want to train, choose movements that remain completely pain-free and reduce the load and range rather than testing the painful press.
